clue.text: Election experts oppose slight changes about term for voters

indicators.note: the preceding two words undergo changes, so their letters are rearranged
a term is an end or limit, so only the final letter of the next word is kept
the rearranged letters go around, or about, the single letter taken from the last word

blocks.note: twelve letters to be reworked
the last letter of voters

explanation.surface: Pundits on polling day are opposed to small swings in how voters are described.
explanation.walkthrough: The S from the end of voters sits inside the jumble of OPPOSE SLIGHT to make PSEPHOLOGISTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Psephology is the statistical study of elections and voting, so its practitioners are specialists in polls.

clue.text: Clasp Spooner's unhealthy looking person from Helsinki?

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner famously swapped the sounds of words, so the phrase is said with its sounds traded

blocks.note: pasty means pale and sickly, and a Finn comes from Finland, whose capital is Helsinki; trading the sounds of the two words gives the clasp

explanation.surface: A sickly-looking Finn grabs hold of something, as Spooner would put it.
explanation.walkthrough: PASTY FINN with its sounds swapped approximates the answer, though it is a loose spoonerism: the S and F trade places as well as the P.
explanation.definitionFit: A safety pin is a bent pin with a guarded point, used as a clasp to fasten fabric.

clue.text: Soft black digit

blocks.note: p is piano, the musical direction for soft
inky means very dark

explanation.surface: A soft, dark-stained finger.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinky is an informal name for the little finger, the smallest digit on the hand.

clue.text: Dropping old glove in centre of Margate

indicators.note: the centre of a seven-letter word is its fourth letter, the only one kept

blocks.note: O is the abbreviation for old
a mitt is a glove, as in baseball
taken as written
the middle letter of Margate

explanation.surface: Someone loses an old glove in the middle of Margate.
explanation.walkthrough: Margate is an English seaside resort in Kent.
explanation.definitionFit: Omitting something means leaving it out, which is what dropping it from a list does.

clue.text: Key batsman facing new ball

blocks.note: first meaning: a device that opens a lock
second meaning: a cricketer who starts the innings

explanation.walkthrough: Key batsman reads as an important player; the words split into two meanings. In cricket, the first two batsmen face the fresh ball at the start of an innings.
explanation.definitionFit: An opener opens things, as a key does, and in cricket it is a batsman who begins the innings.

clue.text: Confine it with dressing!

indicators.note: dressing means arranging or preparing, so these letters are set out afresh

blocks.note: nine letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A nurse's advice: keep a wound contained by bandaging it.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: a dressing on a wound is how you contain the problem the answer names.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandage is used to keep an infected wound sealed, so the clue describes treating germs in a cut.

clue.text: Earth civil engineer's taken from row of houses

indicators.note: taken from means removed from the longer word that follows

blocks.note: CE is the abbreviation for civil engineer
a terrace is a row of joined houses

explanation.surface: A civil engineer has removed soil from a street of houses.
explanation.walkthrough: A terrace is a British row of houses joined side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Terra is Latin for earth, used for the planet in science fiction and in phrases like terra firma.

clue.text: Vehicle in which Nick gets stuck between junction and traffic

indicators.note: stuck between means placed in the middle, flanked by the outer pieces

blocks.note: a fork in a road is a junction
nick and lift both mean steal in British slang
truck means dealings or trade, as in have no truck with

explanation.surface: A vehicle gets jammed in traffic at a junction, and someone named Nick is stuck inside.
explanation.walkthrough: Nick looks like a person's name; it is the British slang verb for steal. Traffic is a verb meaning trade, matching the old sense of truck.
explanation.definitionFit: A forklift truck is a small industrial vehicle with prongs for lifting pallets.

clue.text: Overzealous pogo dancer might combust

blocks.note: first meaning: literally, someone leaping too high strikes the top of the room
second meaning: explode with rage

explanation.walkthrough: Pogo dancing is jumping straight up and down, as punks did. Combust is figurative here, meaning to lose one's temper.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to become suddenly furious, which matches flaring up in anger.

clue.text: Unpleasant drive

blocks.note: first meaning: disagreeable, causing offence
second meaning: a military push or attacking campaign

explanation.walkthrough: Drive here is a noun, as in a concerted attack, not something done in a car.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an adjective for something objectionable and a noun for a forceful military attack.

clue.text: Persian starts to fret as Ruby strokes it

indicators.note: the starts of the following words are their opening letters, which are the only ones kept

blocks.note: the opening letters of these five words

explanation.surface: A Persian cat gets anxious while its owner Ruby pets it.
explanation.walkthrough: Persian looks like a cat in the surface; it is the language.
explanation.definitionFit: Farsi is the language of Iran, also called Persian.

clue.text: Strip by extremely trendy pool

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes of the next word, its first and last letters

blocks.note: a football strip is a team's kit
the outside letters of trendy

explanation.surface: A fashionable swimming pool next to a changing area, or a team kit shown off poolside.
explanation.walkthrough: A strip in British usage is the uniform a sports team wears.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitty is a shared pool of money, as in a card game or office fund.

clue.text: Clear moat with a group of conservationists

blocks.note: a moat is a defensive ditch, a trench
taken as written
the National Trust, the British heritage conservation charity

explanation.surface: Conservation volunteers clean out a castle moat.
explanation.walkthrough: Clear looks like a verb (clear the moat) but is the adjective definition. The National Trust looks after historic houses and land in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Trenchant comments are incisive and forceful, cutting through confusion, so clear and sharp in expression.

clue.text: Distinguished artist's model may say this

blocks.note: first meaning: impressive and dignified in appearance
second meaning: split as two words, a sitter explaining what they are doing

explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as I'M POSING, which is just what an artist's model might announce.
explanation.definitionFit: An imposing figure is grand and commanding in presence, which suits a distinguished person.

clue.text: Compound iodine turns to before initially making another chemical

indicators.note: to compound is to mix together, so the following letters are combined in a new order

blocks.note: I is the chemical symbol for iodine
taken as written
the first letter of the word after, making

explanation.surface: A chemistry lesson: compounded iodine turns into another element.
explanation.walkthrough: Compound looks like a chemistry noun but is the verb mix. Before initially making means the first letter of making comes last in the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Strontium is a metallic element, so it is another chemical alongside iodine.

clue.text: Start to burn a collection of books?

blocks.note: first meaning: to set alight
second meaning: Amazon's e-reader, which holds a whole library

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests book burning; the question mark flags the brand-name e-reader.
explanation.definitionFit: To kindle a fire is to light it, and a Kindle e-reader stores many books digitally.

clue.text: Crumble lots of fertiliser in a river

indicators.note: lots of means most but not all, so the word loses its final letter
in places the shortened word inside the river's name

blocks.note: compost is rotted matter used as fertiliser
the Dee is a river in Wales, England and Scotland

explanation.surface: A heap of manure in a river falls apart.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the T from compost, then sit what remains inside DEE.
explanation.definitionFit: To decompose is to rot and break down, so to crumble into decay.

clue.text: Tailless cat on Roman temple

indicators.note: without a tail, the animal's name loses its last letter

blocks.note: a panther is a big cat
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cat with no tail sits on the steps of a Roman temple.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pantheon in Rome is an ancient domed temple to all the gods.

clue.text: It's plain aunt is angry about medico

indicators.note: an angry relative is worked up and out of order, so her letters are rearranged
the rearranged relative goes around the doctor

blocks.note: the relative's letters, to be mixed
DR is the abbreviation for doctor

explanation.surface: It's obvious that an aunt is furious with the doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: Plain here is a noun, a stretch of flat land, not the adjective meaning obvious.
explanation.definitionFit: Tundra is a vast treeless Arctic plain with permanently frozen subsoil.

clue.text: Good shot behind farm building bags large type of goose

indicators.note: behind says the shot comes after the farm building in the answer
to bag something is to pocket it, so the shot holds the letter for large

blocks.note: a barn is a farm building
an ace is an unreturnable serve in tennis
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A hunter behind the barn bags a big goose with a fine shot.
explanation.walkthrough: Bags reads as a hunter's kill; it means the shot swallows the L.
explanation.definitionFit: The barnacle goose is a black-and-white Arctic species named after an old belief that it grew from barnacles.

clue.text: Green form of transport is what's used in central Guatemala?

indicators.note: central asks for the letters at the very middle of the country's name and nothing else

blocks.note: the middle three of the nine letters of Guatemala

explanation.surface: Asking what green vehicle the people of central Guatemala ride.
explanation.walkthrough: The three letters at the middle of GUATEMALA, described aloud, are 'T and EM', which run together into the answer; that described phrase is the joke.
explanation.definitionFit: A bicycle built for two riders is pedal-powered, so it is an environmentally friendly vehicle.

clue.text: I'm 19 and end up unemployed

indicators.note: things that are up are in turmoil or stirred around, so these letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the answer to 19 across, which speaks as I'm here
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone at number 19 finishes up out of work.
explanation.walkthrough: I'm 19 stands for the answer to 19 across, whose letters join END in the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: A worker made redundant has lost their job because the post is no longer needed, a British term for laid off.

clue.text: German painter displaying one of his articles about old city

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the article goes round the city

blocks.note: der is a German definite article, his being the German painter's
Ur is the ancient city of Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: A German artist shows one of his pieces depicting an ancient city.
explanation.walkthrough: Articles looks like paintings or writings; it is grammar, the German word for the.
explanation.definitionFit: Albrecht Dürer was the great German Renaissance painter and engraver.

clue.text: Animal arrived then left

blocks.note: came means arrived
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A creature turned up and then went away again.
explanation.definitionFit: A camel is a humped desert mammal, a specific example of an animal.

clue.text: Many requests for lots of beer

blocks.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, many
asks means requests

explanation.surface: Plenty of people order a lot of beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Casks are barrels, each holding a large quantity of ale.

clue.text: One after fish bones

indicators.note: after puts the numeral one later in the answer than the fish

blocks.note: a carp is a freshwater fish
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: One person goes after fish bones, picking them out of dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Carpi is the plural of carpus, the group of wrist bones.

clue.text: Use lower gear, as many do on Friday

definitions.text: Use lower gear, as many do on Friday

blocks.note: surface reading: shift a vehicle into a slower gear
setter's reading: gear is clothing, and office workers wear casual clothes at the end of the week

explanation.walkthrough: Gear looks mechanical but means clothes; lower means less formal.
explanation.definitionFit: To dress down is to wear more casual clothing than usual, as on a casual Friday at work.

clue.text: Cabinet-maker?

blocks.note: surface reading: a carpenter who builds cupboards
setter's reading: the person who chooses the senior ministers of a government

explanation.walkthrough: The hyphenated word looks like joinery; the question mark signals the political cabinet.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain the head of government appoints the Cabinet, the senior ministers who run departments.
